1.word_for_word: ūna-triṃśe — in the twenty-ninth chapter; rāsa-artham — for the sake of the rāsa dance; ukti-pratyuktayaḥ hareḥ gopībhiḥ — Hari's statements and the gopīs' replies; rāsa-saṃrambhe — at the commencement of rāsa; tasya ca antardhi-kautukam — and the wonder of his disappearance; brahma-ādi-jaya-saṃrūḍha-darpa-kandarpa-darpahā — destroyer of the pride of Cupid, whose own pride had grown from conquering Brahmā and others; jayati śrī-patiḥ — victorious is the Lord of Śrī; gopī-rāsa-maṇḍala-maṇḍanaḥ — ornament of the circle of gopīs in rāsa; nanu viparītam idam — objection: this seems contradictory; para-dāra-vinodena — by sporting with others' wives; kandarpa-vijetṛtva-pratīteḥ — since this seems to show not victory over Cupid but indulgence; yoga-māyām upāśritaḥ — he resorted to Yogamāyā; ātmārāmaḥ api arīramat — though self-delighting, he caused them to enjoy; sākṣāt manmatha-manmathaḥ — directly the enchanter of Cupid; ātmani avaruddha-saurataḥ — whose erotic power remained contained within himself; svātantrya-abhidhānāt — because these expressions declare his complete independence; rāsa-krīḍā-viḍambanam kāma-vijaya-khyāpanāya — the imitation of erotic rāsa play is to proclaim his conquest of desire; śṛṅgāra-kathā-apadeśena — under the form of an erotic narrative; viśeṣataḥ nivṛtti-parā iyam pañcādhyāyī — these five chapters are especially directed toward renunciation; tāḥ rātrīḥ — those nights; maye imā raṃsyatha kṣapāḥ iti pratiśrutāḥ — the nights promised by Kṛṣṇa when he said ‘you will sport with me on these coming nights’
1.translation: In the twenty-ninth chapter are presented Hari's words and the gopīs' replies concerning the rāsa dance, the beginning of the rāsa celebration, and the wonder of Kṛṣṇa's disappearance. Victory to Śrīpati, ornament of the gopīs' rāsa-circle, who destroyed the pride of Cupid—Cupid whose own arrogance had swelled after conquering Brahmā and others. One may object that sporting with the wives of others seems the opposite of conquering Cupid. Not so. The text says that Kṛṣṇa ‘resorted to Yogamāyā,’ that ‘though self-satisfied he sported,’ that he is ‘the very enchanter of Cupid,’ and that his erotic power was ‘restrained within himself’; these statements explicitly establish his independence from desire. Therefore the true purport is that his enactment of rāsa play proclaims his victory over kāma. Moreover, although these five chapters take the outward form of an erotic narrative, they are especially directed toward detachment; this will become clear. ‘Those nights’ are the nights Kṛṣṇa had previously promised the gopīs when he said, ‘On these coming nights you will sport with me.’

2.word_for_word: tadā tasmin eva kṣaṇe — then, at that very moment; tat-pratītaye — as if to make that promise manifest; uḍu-rāṭ candraḥ udagāt — the king of stars, the moon, arose; dīrgha-kālena darśanam yasya sa priyaḥ — like a beloved seen after a long time; sva-priyāyā mukham aruṇena kuṅkumena vilimpati yathā — as he would anoint his beloved's face with red kuṅkuma; prācyāḥ kakubhaḥ mukham — the face of the eastern direction; śantamaiḥ sukhatamaiḥ karaiḥ — with exceedingly soothing rays; aruṇena udaya-rāgeṇa — with the red glow of rising; aruṇīkurvan — reddening it; carṣaṇīnām śucaḥ tāpa-glānīḥ mṛjan — removing the sorrow, heat and weariness of people
2.translation: At that very moment, as though to make Kṛṣṇa's promise manifest, the moon—the king of stars—rose. Like a lover who, after a long separation, anoints the face of his beloved with red kuṅkuma, the moon colored the face of the eastern quarter with the crimson glow of his rising and with his most soothing rays, while wiping away the sorrow, heat and weariness of living people.

3.word_for_word: kumat kumudam vikasanīyam vidyate yasya — possessing blooming night-lotuses; kumudvantam — adorned with kumudas; na khaṇḍam maṇḍalam yasya — whose orb was unbroken and full; ramāyā ānanasya iva ābhā yasya — whose splendor resembled the face of Lakṣmī; nava-kuṅkumam iva aruṇam — reddish like fresh kuṅkuma; evaṃ-vidham candram dṛṣṭvā — seeing such a moon; vanam ca komalaiḥ gobhiḥ raśmibhiḥ rañjitam — and the forest colored by its soft rays; kalam madhuram jagau — Kṛṣṇa sang sweetly and melodiously; vāma-dṛśām — of the beautiful-eyed women; manoharam yathā — in a manner enchanting their minds
3.translation: He saw the moon adorned with blossoming night-lotuses, its disk full and unbroken, shining like the face of Lakṣmī and reddish like fresh kuṅkuma. He also saw the forest colored by its gentle rays. Then Kṛṣṇa sang a soft, sweet melody, one that irresistibly enchanted the minds of the beautiful-eyed gopīs.

4.word_for_word: asāpatnyāya — so that there would be no rivalry among co-wives; anyonyam alakṣitaḥ na jñāpitaḥ udyamaḥ yābhiḥ — each concealed her departure from the others; sa kāntaḥ yatra — where that beloved was; gīta-dhvani-mārgeṇa ājagmuḥ — they came by following the path of the sound of his song; javena vegena — with speed; lolāni cañcalāni kuṇḍalāni yāsām — their earrings swinging; jagmuḥ iti vaktavye ājagmuḥ — Śuka says ‘came’ rather than merely ‘went’; śukasya kṛṣṇa-antike sva-avasthāna-sphūrteḥ — because Śuka's absorption made him feel himself situated near Kṛṣṇa
4.translation: So that none would become conscious of the others as rivals, each gopī kept the undertaking secret from the rest. Following the sound of Kṛṣṇa's song, they came to the place where their beloved stood, moving so swiftly that their earrings swung from side to side. Śrīdhara notes the use of ‘they came’ rather than simply ‘they went’: Śuka's absorption in the līlā makes him speak as though he himself were situated beside Kṛṣṇa.

5-7.word_for_word: śrī-kṛṣṇa-sūcaka-śabda-śravaṇena — by hearing the sound that signaled Śrī Kṛṣṇa; tat-pravaṇa-cittānām — of those whose minds were wholly inclined toward him; tat-kṣaṇam eva traivargika-karma-nivṛttim — the immediate cessation of acts aimed at the three worldly aims; ardha-avasitam karma vihāya yayuḥ — they left household acts half-finished and went; duhanthyaḥ — some while milking; payaḥ sthālī-stham culliyām adhiśritya — some had placed milk in a pot upon the stove; kvātham apratīkṣamāṇāḥ — without waiting for it to boil; saṃyāvam godhūma-kaṇa-annam — saṃyāva, a cooked wheat preparation; pakvam anudvāsya anuttārya — leaving it cooked but not taken down; pramṛjantyaḥ — some were cleaning or anointing the body; aṅga-udvartana-ādi kurvantyaḥ — engaged in rubbing and bathing; kṛṣṇa-tuṣṭi-artham karma — an act done for Kṛṣṇa's satisfaction; tat-āsakta-manasām anyathā kṛtam api phalati — for minds attached to him, even an act done irregularly bears fruit; vyatyasta — reversed; sthānataḥ svarūpataḥ ca ūrdhva-adho-dhāraṇena viparyayam prāptāni vastra-ābharaṇāni — garments and ornaments put on in wrong places or upside down
5-7.translation: Hearing the sound that signaled Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the women whose minds were wholly directed toward him immediately abandoned acts connected with the ordinary aims of life, leaving their work unfinished. Some left while milking; some had set pots of milk upon the stove and departed without waiting for them to boil; others left cooked wheat preparations without taking them down from the fire. Some abandoned bathing, cleansing or anointing themselves. Śrīdhara adds that when the mind is absorbed in Kṛṣṇa, even an action performed irregularly for his satisfaction bears fruit: in their haste some put garments and ornaments in the wrong places or even upside down.

8.word_for_word: na ca kṛṣṇa-ākṛṣṭa-manasām — for those whose minds had been drawn away by Kṛṣṇa; vighnāḥ prabhavanti — obstacles have no power; tāḥ vāryamāṇāḥ iti — this is shown by ‘although they were being restrained’
8.translation: Obstacles cannot prevail over women whose minds have been drawn by Kṛṣṇa. This is the significance of the statement that they continued toward him even while others tried to restrain them.

9.word_for_word: na labdhaḥ nirgamaḥ yābhiḥ — those who were unable to get out; prāk api tat-bhāvanā-yuktāḥ — already before this they were absorbed in contemplation of him; tadā nitarām dadhyuḥ — at that moment they meditated upon him still more intensely
9.translation: Some were prevented from leaving their homes. They had already been habituated to contemplation of Kṛṣṇa, and now, unable to go outwardly, they meditated upon him with even greater intensity.

10-11.word_for_word: tam paramātmānam kṛṣṇam dhyānataḥ prāptāḥ — attaining Kṛṣṇa, the Paramātman, through meditation; guṇa-mayam deham jahuḥ — they abandoned the body constituted of the guṇas; paramātmā iti jñāna-abhāvāt katham jahuḥ — objection: how could they attain liberation without knowing him as Paramātman; jāra-buddhyā api — even though thinking of him as a paramour; vastu-śaktiḥ buddhim na apekṣate — the intrinsic power of a reality does not depend on the conception of the person approaching it; anyathā matvā api pīta-amṛtavat — like nectar that works even if drunk under a mistaken conception; prārabdha-karma-bandhane sati katham jahuḥ — objection: how could they abandon the body while prārabdha karma remained; sadyaḥ prakṣīṇa-bandhanāḥ — their bonds were exhausted immediately; bhogam antareṇa prārabdham katham kṣīṇam — how could prārabdha end without being experienced; duḥsahaḥ preṣṭha-virahaḥ — unbearable separation from the beloved; tena tīvraḥ tāpaḥ — the intense suffering caused by it; dhutāni aśubhāni — their demerit was shaken away; tat-aprāpti-parama-duḥkha-bhogena pāpam kṣīṇam — sin was exhausted through the supreme pain of not attaining him; acyutasya āśleṣeṇa nirvṛtiḥ — the bliss of embracing Acyuta in meditation; parama-sukha-bhogaḥ — experience of supreme happiness; tayā kṣīṇam maṅgalam puṇya-bandhanam — through that, the binding force of merit was exhausted; niḥśeṣa-karma-kṣayāt — through exhaustion of all karma
10-11.translation: Those who were confined attained Kṛṣṇa, the Paramātman, through meditation and abandoned the material body. An objection arises: they did not conceptually know Kṛṣṇa as the Paramātman, but thought of him as a paramour; how then could that contact liberate them? Śrīdhara answers that the inherent power of a reality does not depend upon one's intellectual conception of it—just as nectar exerts its power even when one drinks it under a mistaken idea. But how could the body fall away while prārabdha karma remained? Their bondage, he says, was exhausted through experience itself. The unbearable anguish of separation from their beloved produced such intense suffering that their demerit was consumed by the experience of not attaining him; conversely, the supreme bliss of embracing Acyuta in meditation exhausted the binding store of their merit. Thus, through the simultaneous exhaustion of all karma in that intense happiness and suffering, they abandoned the guṇa-made body.

12.word_for_word: yathā pati-putra-ādīnām vastutaḥ brahmatve api — although husbands, sons and all beings are ultimately Brahman; na tad-bhajanāt mokṣaḥ — serving them does not automatically give liberation; tathā kṛṣṇe api brahma-buddhi-abhāvena — likewise, if the gopīs did not conceive Kṛṣṇa as Brahman; tat-saṅgatiḥ katham mokṣa-hetuḥ — how could association with him cause liberation; kṛṣṇam viduḥ iti — this objection is raised by the verse; param kevalam kāntam kamaniyam — they knew him simply as their supremely attractive beloved
12.translation: A further objection is raised. Husbands, sons and other beings are, in the ultimate sense, Brahman, yet merely serving them does not produce liberation. So if the gopīs lacked the cognition ‘Kṛṣṇa is Brahman’ and knew him only as a supremely attractive beloved, why should association with him liberate them?

13.word_for_word: pariharati — the objection is answered; jīveṣu āvṛtam brahmatvam — in ordinary living beings their Brahman nature is covered; kṛṣṇasya tu hṛṣīkeśatvāt anāvṛtam — in Kṛṣṇa, being Hṛṣīkeśa, it is uncovered and manifest; ataḥ na tatra buddhi-apekṣā — therefore liberation through him does not depend upon first entertaining the correct conceptual judgment
13.translation: The answer is that in ordinary living beings Brahmanhood is covered, whereas in Kṛṣṇa, Hṛṣīkeśa, it is fully manifest and unobscured. Therefore Kṛṣṇa's liberating power is not dependent on a person's first forming the explicit conceptual judgment that he is Brahman.

14.word_for_word: nanu dehī katham anāvṛtaḥ syāt — objection: how can one who appears embodied be unobscured Brahman; guṇa-ātmanaḥ — of the controller of the guṇas; guṇa-niyantuḥ — the one who governs the qualities; bhagavataḥ evaṃ-rūpā abhivyaktiḥ — this bodily form is Bhagavān's own manifestation; ataḥ na dehī-sādṛśyam — therefore he cannot be equated with an ordinary embodied being
14.translation: If one asks how Kṛṣṇa can be unobscured Brahman while visibly embodied, Śrīdhara answers that he is the controller, not the product, of the guṇas. This form is Bhagavān's own manifestation; hence its apparent embodiment cannot be compared with the conditioned embodiment of an ordinary living being.

15.word_for_word: ataḥ yathā kathañcit tad-āsaktiḥ mukti-kāraṇam — therefore attachment to him in any manner becomes a cause of liberation; kāmam — desire; aikyam — identification or intimate relation; sambandham — relationship; sauhṛdam — friendship/devotion
15.translation: Therefore attachment to Kṛṣṇa, whatever the immediate mode in which it arises, can become a cause of liberation. Śrīdhara glosses the verse's categories: desire, identification or intimate relationship, and friendship or devotion.

16.word_for_word: na ca bhagavataḥ ayam atibhāraḥ — this should not be thought too extraordinary or burdensome for Bhagavān; yataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇāt — because through Śrī Kṛṣṇa; etat sthāvara-ādikam api vimucyate — even stationary beings and the rest are liberated
16.translation: Nor should this liberating effect be thought an excessive claim regarding Bhagavān, for through Śrī Kṛṣṇa even trees and other stationary beings can attain liberation.

17.word_for_word: prastutam āha — Śuka returns to the immediate narrative; tāḥ dṛṣṭvā iti — with ‘seeing them’; vācaḥ-peśaiḥ — with elegant speech; vāk-vilāsaiḥ — playful verbal art; editor note — the following question-and-answer digression would disturb rasa, so Śrīdhara himself eagerly returns to the narrative
17.translation: Śrīdhara now returns to the immediate story with the words ‘seeing them.’ ‘Vācaḥ-peśaiḥ’ means graceful turns of speech or verbal play. The accompanying editorial note observes that the preceding philosophical question-and-answer digression would interrupt the rasa of the rāsa narrative, and that Śrīdhara therefore resumes it with evident eagerness.

18.word_for_word: sarvāḥ sa-sambhramam āgatāḥ vilokya — seeing that all of them had come in agitation and haste; sa-bhayam iva āha — Kṛṣṇa speaks as though apprehensive; vrajasya iti — beginning ‘for Vraja...’
18.translation: Seeing that all the gopīs had come hurriedly and in great agitation, Kṛṣṇa speaks as though concerned for their safety, beginning with his words about Vraja.

19.word_for_word: lajjayā manda-hasitam ālakṣya — noticing their shy, slight smiles; āha — he says; rajanī eṣā iti — ‘this night...’
19.translation: Noticing their faint smiles of embarrassment, Kṛṣṇa continues, ‘This night is…’

20.word_for_word: mātaraḥ iti — with the word ‘mothers’; vicinvanti — they search; mṛgayante — they look for you; bandhūnām sādhvasam kṛcchram mā kṛdhvam — do not cause your relatives fear and distress
20.translation: With the reference to their mothers Kṛṣṇa means: ‘They are searching for you. Do not cause your relatives fear and distress.’

21-22.word_for_word: īṣat-praṇaya-kopena anyataḥ vilokayantīḥ — to the gopīs who looked aside in slight loving anger; dṛṣṭam iti — he says ‘you have seen’; rākeśasya pūrṇa-candrasya karaiḥ rañjitam — colored by the rays of the full moon; yamunā-sparśinaḥ anilasya līlā manda-gatiḥ — the gentle movement of the breeze touching the Yamunā; tayā ejantaḥ kampamānāḥ tarūṇām pallavāḥ — tree shoots trembling in that breeze; taiḥ śobhitam — beautified by them; satīḥ — O virtuous women
21-22.translation: When the gopīs turn their faces aside in a little loving anger, Kṛṣṇa says, ‘You have now seen the forest’—colored by the rays of the full moon and beautified by tender shoots trembling in the slow, playful breeze that has touched the Yamunā. ‘Satīḥ’ is a direct address: ‘O virtuous women.’

23.word_for_word: saṃrambha-kṣubhita-dṛṣṭīḥ — their glances agitated by rising emotion; athavā iti — he changes tack with ‘or rather’; yantrita-āśayāḥ — whose hearts are constrained/captivated; vaśīkṛta-cittāḥ — whose minds have been brought under control; upapannam — fitting, reasonable; prīyante — are pleased
23.translation: Seeing their eyes agitated by emotion, Kṛṣṇa changes his approach: ‘Or rather…’ ‘Yantritāśayāḥ’ means that their hearts had been captivated and brought under his control; ‘upapannam’ means fitting, and ‘prīyante’ means ‘they become pleased.’

24.word_for_word: dṛṣṭa-adṛṣṭa-bhaya-pradarśanena — by showing dangers visible in this world and invisible in the next; nivartayati — he tries to turn them back; bhartuḥ iti-ādi śloka-trayeṇa — in the three verses beginning with duty to the husband
24.translation: Kṛṣṇa now attempts to send them home by pointing out both visible worldly dangers and unseen consequences hereafter, in the three verses beginning with their duty toward the husband.

26.word_for_word: phalgu — trivial; tuccham — insignificant; kṛcchram — difficult to obtain, troublesome; aupapatyam — the pleasure of adultery/paramour love
26.translation: ‘Phalgu’ means trivial or worthless; ‘kṛcchra’ means difficult and troublesome to obtain; ‘aupapathya’ means the pleasure of a paramour relationship.

27.word_for_word: kiṃ ca — moreover; śravaṇāt iti — this further point is made in the verse beginning ‘by hearing’
27.translation: Kṛṣṇa adds a further argument in the verse beginning with the statement about hearing.

29.word_for_word: cintām prāptānām sthitim āha — he describes the condition of the gopīs as they fell into anxiety; śucaḥ śokāt udgatena śvasanena — by sighs arising from grief; śuṣyantaḥ bimba-phala-sadṛśāḥ adharāḥ — their bimba-fruit-like lips dried up; mukhāni avāñci kṛtvā — lowering their faces; aṅguṣṭhena mahīm likhantyaḥ — tracing the ground with a toe; gṛhīta-kajjalaḥ aśrubhiḥ — with tears carrying away their collyrium; kuca-kuṅkumāni kṣālayantyaḥ — washing the kuṅkuma from their breasts; tūṣṇīm sthitāḥ — standing silent; uru-duḥkhasya bharaḥ yāsām — burdened by immense sorrow
29.translation: Śuka describes their state when anxiety overtook them. Sighs born of grief dried their bimba-red lips. They lowered their faces and traced the earth with their toes; their tears, darkened with eye-collyrium, washed away the kuṅkuma upon their breasts. Bearing the weight of immense sorrow, they stood in silence.

30.word_for_word: kiñcit saṃrambhena kopa-āveśena — with a little agitation and anger; gadgadā giraḥ — voices choked; tāḥ abruvata — they spoke; saṃrambhe kāraṇam — the reason for their indignation; preṣṭham — their dearest beloved; priya-itaram iva pratibhāṣamāṇam — speaking like someone unfriendly; pratyācakṣāṇam — apparently rejecting them
30.translation: Then, with a touch of angry agitation and voices choked by emotion, they spoke. The cause of their indignation was that the one dearest to them was speaking as though he were unfriendly and seemed to be rejecting them.

31.word_for_word: nṛśaṃsam — cruel, pitiless; he duravagraha — O difficult-to-restrain one, O independent one; svacchanda — acting by your own will; tava pāda-mūlam bhaktāḥ — we who are devoted to the root of your feet; sevitavatīḥ asmān — who have come to serve you; bhajasva — accept, reciprocate with; mā tyaja — do not abandon
31.translation: ‘Do not speak so cruelly, O utterly independent one. We have devoted ourselves to your feet and have come to serve you. Accept us; do not abandon us.’

32.word_for_word: yat uktam pati-apatya-ādi tvayā dharma-vidā — what you, knower of dharma, said about husbands, children and the rest; sa-upahāsam eva — they answer with irony; etat upadeśānām pade viṣaye tvayi eva astu — let all such injunctions find their true object in you yourself; īśa — because you are the Lord; sarva-upadeśānām īśa-paratva-avagamāt — all teachings ultimately point toward the Lord; ātmā kila bhavān — you are indeed the Self; bhogyasya sarvasya bhoktā ātmā eva īśaḥ — the Self is the true enjoyer and ruler of all that is enjoyed; preṣṭhaḥ bandhuḥ ca bhavān eva — thus you alone are the dearest relative; alternative 1: dharma-upadeṣṭari tvayi sati — if you are taken as the teacher of dharma; asmāsu dharmam jijñāsamānāsu — and us as women asking about dharma; yad uktam etat astu — let the instruction stand, but you are more than merely a teacher: you are the Self; alternative 2: upadeśa-pade tad-gocare puruṣe astu — let the rule apply to ordinary persons who are objects of such instruction; tvayi tu īśe — but not in the same way to you, the Lord; alternative 3: pati-ādi-śuśrūṣaṇam dharma iti — the rule ‘service to husband and others is dharma’; tvayi eva astu — is fulfilled in you; pati-ādīnām pade adhiṣṭhāne — because you are the basis in whom husband, children and all others subsist; na īśvaram adhiṣṭhānam vinā kaḥ api pati-putra-ādiḥ — without the Lord as their ground, no husband or son exists independently; alam ati-vistareṇa — enough of excessive elaboration
32.translation: The gopīs answer Kṛṣṇa's instruction about serving husband, children and relatives with deliberate irony: ‘You are a knower of dharma; let everything you have just taught find its proper fulfillment in you.’ Śrīdhara gives several closely related readings. First, all injunctions ultimately terminate in the Lord, and Kṛṣṇa is that Lord. He is also the true Self, the ultimate enjoyer of everything enjoyed; therefore he alone is the dearest relative, and duties owed to all relatives ultimately rest in him. Alternatively, if Kṛṣṇa is treated merely as a teacher of dharma and the gopīs as students asking about dharma, his instruction may stand—but he is not merely a teacher; he is their very Self. Again, the ordinary rule may apply to ordinary men who are the proper objects of such social injunctions, but Kṛṣṇa is the supreme Lord and cannot be placed on the same level. Finally, even the rule ‘serving one's husband and family is dharma’ is ultimately fulfilled in serving Kṛṣṇa, because he is the supporting ground in whom husbands, sons and every other relative subsist; apart from the Lord as their foundation, none of them exists independently. Śrīdhara ends: enough of elaborating the alternatives.

33.word_for_word: etat sad-ācāreṇa dṛḍhayantyaḥ — they strengthen this point by citing the conduct of the wise; prārthayante — and pray; kuśalāḥ — skillful, wise; śāstra-nipuṇāḥ — expert in scripture; kiṃ prajayā kariṣyāmaḥ yeṣām naḥ ayam ātmā ayam ca lokaḥ — ‘what shall we do with offspring, for whom this Self and this world are ours?’
33.translation: They reinforce their argument by appealing to the conduct of those truly expert in scripture and pray accordingly. Śrīdhara cites the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad: ‘What shall we do with offspring, when for us this Self is all and this world is all?’

34.word_for_word: pratiyāta iti yad uktam — your instruction ‘return home’; tat aśakyam — is impossible; tvayā eva cittādīnām apahṛtatvāt — because you yourself have stolen our minds and faculties; yat asmākam cittam etāvantam kālam sukhen gṛheṣu nirviśati — our mind that until now comfortably entered household life; tat tvayā apahṛtam — has been taken by you; karau api yau gṛhya-kṛtye nirviśataḥ — our two hands that once entered household duties; tau api — those too have been taken away; sukhātmanā tvayā iti vā — alternatively, ‘by you whose nature is bliss’
34.translation: ‘You tell us to return home, but that is impossible because you yourself have stolen the very faculties by which we could live there. The mind that until now settled comfortably into household life has been taken away by you; even the hands that once performed our domestic duties are no longer ours to command.’ Alternatively, the expression may stress that all this has been done by Kṛṣṇa whose very nature is bliss.

35.word_for_word: he kṛṣṇa — O Kṛṣṇa; naḥ hṛc-chaya-agniḥ — the fire of desire in our hearts; tava adhara-amṛta-pūrakeṇa — with the nectar flowing from your lips; tava eva hāsa-sahitena avalokena — by your smiling glance; kala-gītena ca — and by your sweet song; jātaḥ — has arisen; tam siñca — pour upon it, quench it; no cet — otherwise; virahāt janiṣyate yaḥ agniḥ — the fire that will arise from separation; tena upayukta-dehāḥ dagdha-śarīrāḥ — our bodies consumed by it; yoginaḥ iva — like yogins; te padavīm antikam dhyānena yāma — through meditation we shall attain your presence
35.translation: ‘O Kṛṣṇa, the fire of desire in our hearts was kindled by your own smiling glances, your sweet song and the nectar of your lips. Quench it with that same nectar. Otherwise the further fire born of separation will consume our bodies, and like yogins who leave the body in contemplation, we shall reach your presence through meditation.’

36.word_for_word: nanu sva-patīn eva upagacchata — objection: go back to your husbands; te enam agnim siñceyuḥ — let them quench this fire; ramāyā lakṣmyā datta-kṣaṇam — you to whom Lakṣmī grants an occasion; datta-utsavam datta-avasaram vā — grants a festival or opportunity; tat api kvacit eva na sarvadā — even she receives that only occasionally, not always; araṇya-janāḥ priyāḥ yasya — you who love the people of the forest; araṇye kvacit yarhi aspṛkṣma — once, in the forest, we touched you; tvayā abhiramitāḥ ānanditāḥ — you delighted us; tat ārabhya anya-samakṣam sthātum api na pārayāmaḥ — since then we cannot even remain in the presence of other men; tucchāḥ te na rocante — they seem insignificant and give us no delight
36.translation: If Kṛṣṇa's implication is, ‘Return to your husbands and let them relieve this longing,’ the gopīs answer: even Lakṣmī receives intimate opportunity with him only at certain times. Kṛṣṇa is especially fond of the forest-dwellers. ‘Once we touched you here in the forest and you filled us with joy. From that moment onward we have been unable even to stand comfortably in the presence of other men; they seem utterly insignificant to us.’

37.word_for_word: tvat-pāda-saubhāgyam ati-citram — the fortune of your feet is exceedingly wondrous; śrīḥ — Lakṣmī; vakṣasi asāpatnyam sthānam labdhvā api — although she has an unrivaled place upon your chest; tulasyā sapatnyā saha — together with Tulasī, as though her co-wife; tava pāda-ambuja-rajaḥ kāmayate sma — she desires the dust of your lotus feet; bhṛtyaiḥ sarvaiḥ juṣṭam — that dust is served by all your servants; yasyāḥ sva-vīkṣaṇa-kṛte — for whose own glance; brahma-ādīnām tapobhiḥ prayāsaḥ — Brahmā and other gods undergo austerity simply to obtain her glance; sā tat-rajaḥ prapannā — that very Lakṣmī seeks your foot-dust; tadvat vayam api — likewise do we
37.translation: ‘The fortune contained in the dust of your feet is astonishing. Lakṣmī already possesses an unrivaled place upon your chest, yet even she, together with Tulasī as though accepting a co-wife, desires the dust of your lotus feet—the dust cherished by all your servants. Brahmā and the other gods undergo austerities merely in the hope that Lakṣmī will glance upon them, yet she herself seeks your foot-dust. We too have surrendered to that same dust.’

38.word_for_word: he vṛjina-ardana — O destroyer of suffering/sin; tvat-upāsane tvat-bhajane eva āśā yāsām — we whose only hope is worship and service of you; vasatīḥ gṛhān visṛjya — abandoning our dwellings and homes; yoginaḥ iva prāptāḥ — we have come like yogins who renounce everything; tava sundara-smita-vilasita-nirīkṣaṇena — through your beautiful smiling, playful glance; tīvraḥ kāmaḥ — intense desire; tena tapta-cittānām — our hearts scorched by it; he puruṣa-ratna — O jewel among men; dāsyam dehi — grant us service; textual note alternative negative division — a variant syntactic division could read that they did not arrive merely by abandoning home; the positive reading is adopted in context
38.translation: ‘O destroyer of suffering, our only hope lies in worshiping and serving you. Leaving our homes behind, we have come like renunciant yogins. Your beautiful, playful smile and glance have scorched our hearts with intense longing. O jewel among men, grant us the position of your servants.’ The source also records an alternative syntactic division of the opening expression, but the contextual reading is the affirmative prayer just given.

39.word_for_word: gṛha-svāmyam vihāya dāsyam kim iti prārthyate — why do they pray for servitude after leaving the status of mistresses of homes; alakā-āvṛta-mukham — your face partly covered by curls; kuṇḍalayoḥ śrīḥ yayoh te gaṇḍa-sthale — cheeks beautified by earrings; adhare sudhā — nectar upon the lips; dṛṣṭvā — seeing this face; datta-abhayam bhuja-daṇḍa-yugmam — the pair of arms that grants fearlessness; vakṣaḥ ca śriyā ekam eva ramaṇam — the chest, the unique pleasure-place of Lakṣmī; rati-janakam — awakening love; dāsya eva bhavāmaḥ — we can only become your servants
39.translation: Why, after leaving their positions as mistresses of households, do they ask to become servants? Because, they say, after seeing Kṛṣṇa's face framed by curling locks, his cheeks made beautiful by earrings, the nectar upon his lips, the two strong arms that grant fearlessness, and his chest—the unique abode of Śrī and a source of love—they can desire no status except service to him.

40.word_for_word: nanu jugupsitam aupapatyam iti uktam — objection: Kṛṣṇa had called paramour love contemptible; kā strī iti — they answer with ‘what woman?’; kala-padam — containing sweet notes; āyatam dīrgham mūrcchitam svara-ālāpa-bhedaḥ — long, sustained, modulated melodic phrases; pāṭhāntare kala-padāmṛta-mayam veṇu-gītam — variant reading: flute-song made of nectar-like sweet notes; tena sammohitā — enchanted by it; kā vā strī ārya-caritān nija-dharmān na calet — what woman would not move away from conventional noble conduct and her ordinary duties; yat-mohitāḥ puruṣā api calitāḥ — even men have been moved by it; trailokya-saubhagam — beauty capable of enchanting the three worlds; tvat-dyotaka-śabda-śravaṇa-mātreṇa api — merely by hearing a sound that reveals you; tāvat nija-dharma-tyāgaḥ yuktaḥ — abandoning ordinary duty becomes understandable; kim punaḥ tvat-anubhavena — how much more after directly experiencing you
40.translation: Kṛṣṇa had condemned paramour love as disgraceful, so the gopīs answer: ‘What woman could hear the long, sweet, modulated phrases of your flute and remain unmoved from ordinary social conduct? Even men are transformed by that sound.’ A variant reading speaks of the flute-song as nectar made of sweet musical syllables. Kṛṣṇa possesses the beauty of all three worlds: if merely hearing a sound that announces him can loosen ordinary obligations, how much more should direct experience of him do so?

42.word_for_word: viklavitam — speech born of helpless agitation; pāravaśya-pralapitam — utterance produced by complete emotional dependence; gopīḥ arīramat — he caused the gopīs to enjoy; ramayām āsa — he delighted them
42.translation: ‘Viklavitam’ means speech uttered in helpless emotional agitation. Having heard them, Kṛṣṇa delighted the gopīs and granted the enjoyment for which they had come.

43.word_for_word: priyasya īkṣaṇena utphullāni mukhāni yāsām — their faces blossomed under the beloved's glance; udāra-hāsaḥ — his generous, radiant smile; dvijāḥ — teeth; teṣu kunda-kusumavat dīdhitiḥ — shining like jasmine flowers; eṇāṅkaḥ — the deer-marked moon
43.translation: Their faces blossomed beneath the glance of their beloved. Kṛṣṇa's broad smile revealed teeth shining like jasmine blossoms, while above them shone the deer-marked moon.

46.word_for_word: bāhu-prasāraḥ — spreading his arms; parirambhaḥ — embraces; kara-ādīnām ālabhanam sparśaḥ — touching their hands and limbs; narma — joking; parihāsaḥ — playful banter; nakha-agra-pātaḥ — touches with the tips of his nails; kṣvelyā krīḍayā — through playful sport; avalokaiḥ ca hasitaiḥ ca — with glances and smiles; kāmam tāsām uddīpayan — increasing their love/desire; tāḥ ramayām āsa — he delighted them
46.translation: Kṛṣṇa delighted them by opening his arms, embracing them, touching their hands and limbs, speaking playful jokes, brushing them with the tips of his nails, and sporting with them through affectionate glances and smiles, all of which intensified their love.

47.word_for_word: mahātmanaḥ — from the great Self; vimukta-cittāt — whose mind is wholly free/unbound
47.translation: The expression describes Kṛṣṇa as the great Self whose consciousness is completely free and unattached.

48.word_for_word: tat-saubhagena — because of the extraordinary good fortune of receiving him; madam — intoxication, a sense of independence; asvādhīnatām — the feeling that they were no longer dependent; mānam — pride; garvam — arrogance; keśavaḥ — Keśava; kaḥ ca īśaḥ ca tau vaśayati iti — etymologically, he who brings Ka/Brahmā and Īśa/Śiva under control; antardhāna context — he removed their pride by disappearing
48.translation: The extraordinary fortune of Kṛṣṇa's intimate company produced in some of the gopīs a subtle intoxication—a feeling of self-sufficiency—and ‘māna,’ pride. Keśava, he who can bring even Ka (Brahmā) and Īśa (Śiva) under his control, therefore brought their pride under control by withdrawing himself. Thus ends Śrīdhara Svāmī's Bhāvārtha-dīpikā on Chapter Twenty-nine.
